memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it. — Gen 2:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a truth that surprises many people: work came before sin entered the world. We often think of work as a burden, part of the curse, something we endure until the weekend. But long before Adam ever sinned, God gave him a job—to work the garden and take care of it. Work is not a punishment. It is a gift, woven into God's good design for us from the very beginning.

Notice the two words used: to work it and to take care of it. God gave the man purposeful labour, and also the responsibility to protect and nurture what he had been given. We are made to be productive and to be caretakers. There is deep dignity in this. Whether you tend a field, run a home, sit in a classroom, drive a vehicle, or work in an office, your daily labour matters to God.

It is true that after the fall, work became hard and often frustrating (Gen 3:17–19). Thorns entered the picture. But the goodness of work itself was never cancelled.

In Christ, our work finds its truest meaning. Scripture tells us to work as though for the Lord and not merely for people (Col 3:23). Whatever your hands find to do today, offer it to God. Ordinary work, done faithfully, becomes worship.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you see your daily work as a burden, or as a gift from God?
- How might your attitude change if you worked "for the Lord"?
- In what ordinary task today could you honour God through faithfulness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord God, thank You that work is Your good gift and not a punishment. Help me to labour faithfully in whatever You have given me, doing it for You, so that even my ordinary tasks become worship. Amen.
